text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Agreement on the introduction of a goods and services tax has been reached by business, welfare and community groups at the weekend's tax summit. Consensus was reached on other tax reforms as well, prompting fresh denials from the Government and the Opposition that they would support a GST. Page 3.

Coles Myer chief executive Peter Bartels will stay on at the retailing giant until July next year following the signing of a new contract. Coles chairman Nobby Clark said the performance of Bartels and other senior executives would continue to be evaluated. Bartels announced the company's worst earnings performance in eight years, with the net profit slumping 33.18 per cent to A$280 million. Page 18.

The Federal Government's industrial relations platform look likely to come away from negotiations with the Australian Democrats relatively unchanged, the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry said. A spokeswoman for Democrats Leader Cheryl Kernot said talks were still continuing. Page 7.

Through a joint venture with Australis Media Ltd, Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd is set to expand directly into the telephony and data transmission business. The deal forms part of Australis Media's refinancing plan which was kick-started last week with an agreement by Australis bondholders to allow the company to attempt to raise US$150 million through a junk bond issue in the US. Page 17.

Despite uncertain demand from banks, American Express will forge ahead with a plan to use banks to distribute its charge cards and credit cards. The plan holds possibility for an increase in competition in the payment card market, particularly among high volume users who make little use of the revolving credit on their bank-issued credit card. Page 23.

Proposed Government tax reforms have been rejected by the financial industry. The industry said that reforms to interest withholding tax legislation represent a tightening of the existing regime. The complaint was made in conjunction with a formal joint submission by five key industry groups to the Australian Taxation Office, accusing them of confusing the Government's objectives by narrowly interpreting the proposed legislative changes. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Securities Commission executive director Geoff Shelly has confirmed the ASC's interest in Australian National Industries Ltd's Part A statement to promote its successful A$190 million cash and scrip takeover of Palmer Tube Mills Ltd, but said it would be a few weeks before any further action was warranted. Page 17.

KPN chief executive Wim Dik said yesterday that takeover target TNT Ltd would cooperate with the Australian Securities Commission in their investigation of concerns expressed by the Australian Stock Exchange over heavy options trades before the launch of PN's takeover bid for TNT. Page 17.

Strong demand from overseas investors has pushed National Mutual's final institutional share price above the expected price range of A$1.35 to A$1.55 to A$1.60, meaning more than 500,000 private investors in tomorrow's A$2.7 billion float of the insurer are heading for an instant profit. Page 17.

Due to declining beer sales since the late 1980s, beer marketers, such as those at Lion Nathan, are looking into developing beers with fashionable imagery and premium pricing rather than selling mainstream beer brands to the blue-collar Aussie bloke in a effort to crack Australia's A$6 million premium beer market. Page 17.

Following satellite pay-TV operator Australis Media's announcement on Friday that it would go ahead with the roadshow for its critical A$190 million note issue after securing an additional US$5 million in equity financing, managing director Neil Gamble said he was confident of a warm reception from US investors today. Page 19.

Germany's KirchGroup, one of the biggest broadcasters in Europe said on Friday it paid A$81 million for 7.5 per cent stake in the Packer family's part-owned New Regency movie studio, in a deal which values the Hollywood studio at more than A$1076 million.Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

More than 600 institutions from around the world have driven the institutional share price to A$1.60 and produced a healthy payout for policyholders who chose to take a cash option rather than shares. Page 31.

After being hit by structural change and a cyclical slowdown, manufacturing is yet again, according to numerous dispatches from the frontline of Australian industry, shouldering the burden of economic adjustment and doing it the toughest. Page 31.

Oil industry analysts are openly tipping newly floated Tap Oil as the next takeover target in the oil and gas sector, which during the past nine months has generated a high level of corporate activity, in a move likely to shorten its life as a publicly lised company to only a few months. Page 31.

Coles Myer chief executive Peter Bartels has refused to comment on the part he played in the Yannon transaction, which cost Coles Myer A$18 million, amid calls to release details of the deal before the company's annual general meeting in November. Page 33

Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chair Allan Fels told Channel Nine's Business Sunday program yesterday a court decision allowing Super League to go ahead in Australia has strengthened the ACCC's position with many industries, saying it was "good, strong decision". Page 33.

Dutch group KPN chief executive Wim Dik told the Business Sunday program yesterday an Australian Securities Commission investigation into the A$2 million takeover bid for transport giant TNT by KPN will not affect the deal. KPN's bid for TNT was announced last Wednesday. Page 33.
THE AGE

National Mutual Holdings is set to become one of the country's top 30 quoted companies on the eve of its stockmarket debut tomorrow with a value of A$2.7 billion or more. Even after pricing its shares to institutions at A$1.60, NMH has been swamped by institutional demand from around the world. Page C1.

In the clearest sign of his determination to break up the Gas & Fuel, Victorian Treasurer Alan Stockdale has admitted he is keen to split up the company ahead of a possible A$2 billion privatisation, despite being advised by the Collins Hill Group last yer to keep it whole. Page C1.

After the Wall Street rally on Friday fed on a small but unexpected payroll employment to push the Dow Jones Index to just short of 6000, Australia's stock market is poised to test its all-time high this week. Page C1.

In what will be the world's third biggest initial stock sale, Deutshce Telecom AG could be worth almost A$50 billion when it goes public with its sale next month. The sale was officially kick-started yesterday when the company filed papers saying it planned to sell 20 per cent to the public. Page C3.

An appeal against a recent ruling by a New South Wales court will be launched by the Australian Taxation Office. The ruling, concerning superannuation payments to independent contractors, was handed down three weeks ago by the New South Wales Court of Appal - meaning employers of contractors were not required to pay the superannuation guarantee charge. Page C4.

Despite claims by politicians, bankers and economists that Australian business is in good shape, top manufacturers are putting the squeeze on their marketing and advertising budgets. AIM Data figures for the six months to June show that, while the top 20 dvertisers are still spending, overall expenditure is no more than last year. Page C2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
